title: ACE Workspace (the "ace" key in package.json)
description: Validates the object at manifest.ace in package.json. Describes the agentic coding environment (orchestrator, roles, adapters, models, policies, runtime state) — not application source. Every field below is optional except spec and name: an ace/v1 package written before governance existed still validates.

modelSelection.description: One model/provider route entry. Provider names are validated in code against lib/adapters/index.mjs, never frozen here, so the registry stays swappable.

routeChain.description: Primary route plus the fallbacks that may replace it during recovery. Fallbacks are validated before they are installed, so a chain of unusable routes surfaces as an escalation instead of a silent switch.

supervisor.description: A project execution owner. One supervisor per project.

workspace.description: Workspace root this supervisor's workers may write to, relative to the package unless absolute.

runtime.description: Coding-agent runtime for this supervisor (see adapters.agent-runtime).

heartbeat_seconds.description: How often this supervisor is expected to heartbeat.

worker.description: A bounded implementer. Workers report evidence; they never redefine the goal.

project.description: Owning project. Defaults to the first supervisor's project.

adapterSelection.description: Selects the implementation for one swappable capability.

provider.description: Adapter name from lib/adapters/index.mjs for this kind. Swap it here; the core resolves through the contract.

workers.description: The ace/v1 native worker declaration. Governance reads this when roles.workers is absent.

models.description: Default model selection and per-role route chains. routes.<role> is either a primary+fallbacks object or an ordered array; a primary is tried first and each fallback is validated before it is installed during recovery.

mode.description: Security-relevant. "restricted" denies outbound connections unless an action is explicitly allowed; a lower-trust layer may not loosen this once a higher-authority layer has set it.
Security-relevant. "workspace" bounds reads and writes to the workspace root; widening it from a project or task layer is refused.

worktrees.description: Allow one git worktree per independent task.

push.description: Security-relevant. Push is denied unless this is explicitly true.

require_review_before_merge.description: Security-relevant. A lower-trust layer may not turn this off once a higher-authority layer required it.

access.description: Security-relevant alias of policies.production_access. Denied by default.

entry.description: Workspace document entry points (role to relative path). Like npm main/bin/scripts but for the agentic workspace documents.

default_agent_limit.description: Declared default for the active-agent limit. The value actually enforced is concurrency.max_active_agents.

goal.description: The project's declared main goal. The governor reports alignment against this instead of inventing one.

statement.description: One sentence describing what this project is for.

roles.description: The Governor → Supervisor → Worker hierarchy. The governor may message supervisors only; worker-level action is requested through the responsible supervisor.

scope.description: What the governor oversees — "environment" for every project in this package.

idle_mode.description: What the governor does when no useful work remains: monitor, maintenance or stop.

concurrency.description: The active-agent budget, enforced centrally across every runtime so two runtimes cannot each spend it.

max_active_agents.description: Four is the shipped default, not a hard maximum: raising it is a supported configuration.

count_governor.description: Whether the governor counts toward the budget. Default false.

count_supervisors.description: Whether supervisors count toward the worker budget. Default false.

runtime_overrides.description: Additional per-runtime caps. Both the global limit and the runtime cap must pass.

enforce_across_runtimes.description: When false the budget is reported but not enforced. Default true.

allow_project_raise.description: Whether a project or task layer may raise the limit above an installation-pinned one.

pinned_limit.description: An installation-level ceiling that project raises may not exceed unless allow_project_raise is true.

recovery.description: Bounding rules for liveness detection, progress verification and failover.

stale_heartbeat_seconds.description: A heartbeat older than this makes an agent unresponsive.

progress_window_seconds.description: Window used to decide whether a live agent is actually progressing. A fresh heartbeat alone never proves progress.

cooldown_seconds.description: Minimum gap between recovery actions on the same subject.

lease_seconds.description: Lease TTL used to keep exactly one owner per task and per route.

adapters.description: One provider per swappable capability. The reference configuration uses herdr, git-worktree, acc, proagents and opencode, but every one of them can be replaced here.

watchdog.description: The independent control plane that recovers or escalates a failed governor. It acts without the governor's model.

interval_seconds.description: How often the watchdog inspects the governor.

restarts_allowed.description: Bounded restarts before it escalates to the operator.

delivery.description: How a restart is delivered on this host. Without a delivery function the watchdog records the action and escalates instead of claiming a restart.

sharing.description: Cross-project context and messages are refused unless this is "shared".

verification.description: What must be true before a task may be integrated.

checks.description: Checks re-run after integration. Passing in a worker's isolated workspace does not prove the integrated project passes.

require_evidence.description: A completion claim without a reported command that exited 0 is rejected.

management_bots.description: Experimental management-bot sidecar. Off by default. An enabled bot submits work through ACE, which stays authoritative for task ids, budgets, isolation, verification and audit; a bot can never launch a second group of agents that bypasses the budget.

enabled.description: Off by default. This feature is experimental; nothing is accepted until it is explicitly enabled and the connection fields below are complete.

provider.description: Management-bot provider. GitBot is the default selection once the feature is explicitly enabled. See lib/adapters/index.mjs.

endpoint.description: Inbound endpoint. Missing or partial security configuration fails closed.

identity.description: The identity this bot is expected to present.

secret_ref.description: Name of the stored secret (see `ace secret set`). Secrets are referenced by name, never inlined.

allow_remote_endpoint.description: Explicit opt-in required before a non-loopback endpoint is accepted. Off by default because the default provider documents no authentication of its own; a remote endpoint additionally requires HTTPS and a secret_ref.

projects.description: Inbound project identifier to ACE project mapping. An unmapped project is refused.

permissions.description: Operations the bot may request. A wildcard is refused.

approvals.description: Requested actions that require an explicit approval before a task is created.

description: Validates the object at manifest.ace in package.json.
